objective.statement: The clock widget on HomeView can show the time of a major city around the world, chosen by the user from a dropdown.

complexity.rationale: Time zone aware formatting in the pure helper, a new select in the Clock component and a fixed city list; no dependency, store or contract change.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The Clock widget contains a dropdown (select) with a visible label that lets the user choose a major city.
Choosing a city makes the clock show the current time in that city's IANA time zone, using the existing HH:MM.SS pattern and the selected 12/24 hour view.
The default selection is the browser's local time, so the existing behaviour and tests are unchanged until the user picks a city.
The dropdown offers a fixed list of major cities across the world's regions, each mapped to an IANA time zone, so daylight saving is handled by the platform.
The clock still ticks every second and clears its timer on unmount after a city is chosen.

in.statement: An optional time zone argument on formatClock, a world city list in src/lib, and a city dropdown in the Clock component with local state, plus colocated tests.

out.statement: Multiple simultaneous clocks, free-text city search, persisting the choice, store changes, new dependencies, date display, e2e tests, changes to other HomeView behaviour.

observations.statement: The city list is a fixed set of about 20 major cities (for example London, New York, Tokyo, Sydney); the owner did not name cities.
The selection resets to local time on reload; it stays component-local state and is not written to Zustand or localStorage, matching the existing 12/24 choice.
The first option is 'Local time' so the user can return to the browser time zone; the card does not forbid it and existing tests rely on local time.
Follow ThemePicker's select pattern, data-id test ids in Clock.testIds.ts, AAA test layout, no any, and keep the existing Clock and formatClock tests unchanged.
Intl.DateTimeFormat time zone support must work in the Node test runtime; unit tests use fixed UTC instants and zones without ambiguous daylight saving edges.

provenance.source: New Feature request: A World Clock - make the clock widget on HomeView.tsx changeable to a major city timezone around the world, using a dropdown for the city choice

capabilityOwners.rationale: The selected city is component-local useState next to the existing hour cycle state.
Not used: nothing else needs the city and it is not persisted (o-2).
No remote data in this slice.

unit.rationale: Time zone conversion in formatClock and the city list shape are isolated pure logic.

component.rationale: The dropdown, the zone switch and the retained tick are component behaviour.

integration.rationale: No cross-module or API flow; npm run test is run as regression.

e2e.rationale: Small self-contained widget change with no new route; component tests cover the behaviour.

increments.behavior: formatClock accepts an optional IANA time zone and returns the time in that zone in 24h and 12h; WORLD_CITIES lists major cities with time zones.
Clock shows a labelled city dropdown defaulting to local time; choosing a city shows that city's time.
increments.doneWhen: t-2 passes and the full suite stays green.

tests.description: formatClock with a time zone: Tokyo 24h and 12h, New York, and a half-hour zone (Kolkata); WORLD_CITIES entries have a label and a valid IANA zone.
tests.command: npx vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts src/lib/formatClock.unit.test.ts src/lib/worldCities.unit.test.ts

tests.description: Clock renders a labelled city select defaulting to local time, shows the chosen city's time, honours the 12 hour toggle, and keeps ticking.

expectedRedEvidence.expectedFailure: worldCities module does not exist and formatClock ignores the time zone argument.
expectedRedEvidence.command: npx vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts src/lib/formatClock.unit.test.ts src/lib/worldCities.unit.test.ts
expectedRedEvidence.observedFailure: worldCities import failed to resolve (suite did not load); 4 of 10 formatClock tests failed because the time zone was ignored

expectedRedEvidence.expectedFailure: Clock has no city select, so lookups by the new data-id fail.
expectedRedEvidence.observedFailure: 5 of 12 Clock tests failed: no label City and no element with data-id clock-city-select

verification.requirement: npm run test, npm run lint and npm run build pass.
verification.command: npm run test; npm run lint; npm run build
verification.result: unit 30/30, component 45/45 passed; eslint clean; tsc and vite build succeeded
